title: A Songbook for the Bakery
premise: Rafael Okafor, a pastry chef drowning in debt, discovers her late grandmother's orchard deed lists two names she never expected: her own and that of her estranged first love, Marisol Vega, a corporate lawyer sent to acquire the land for the developer threatening Rafael's café. Forced to share the property neither can sell alone, they spend one harvest season untangling old wounds, family secrets about why the deed was written this way, and the growing truth that duty to their families has cost them both everything. When Marisol must choose between the promotion built on Rafael's ruin and testifying against her own firm, she risks her career to save the orchard; Rafael, in turn, finally lends her whole heart instead of pieces. They end not with the café or the orchard saved by luck, but rebuilt together as a bakery-and-cider house on the land, love chosen over safety.
about_author: R. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love letters on order tickets before turning to fiction. Coldharbour writes romances set in kitchens and small towns where food is the language people use when honesty fails.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A bank letter arrives during morning service at the failing café, and Rafael bakes through panic, hiding the debt from everyone including her business partner. Emotional beat: denial dressed as competence, establishing what she stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Tin
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Clearing her grandmother's kitchen, Rafael finds the orchard deed inside an old biscuit tin — with her name and Marisol Vega's printed side by side. Emotional beat: shock and dread, the past arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Table
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol arrives in town representing Corvane Development, tasked with acquiring the orchard, only to learn the holdout owner is Rafael. Emotional beat: professional armor cracking at the sight of the woman she left ten years ago.

chapters.title: Terms of Co-Ownership
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. The lawyer explains neither can sell without the other's signature; Marisol proposes buying Rafael out, Rafael refuses. Emotional beat: stalemate as flirtation disguised as negotiation.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finds letters suggesting her grandmother deliberately named both women, betting on reconciliation. Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger at being manipulated by the dead.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Storm damage forces them to work the orchard together to protect its appraised value; Marisol rediscovers the physical joy of the place. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness under shared labor.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Over cider after harvest day, they almost kiss; Rafael retreats, confessing she only ever lends pieces of herself. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered then snatched back.

chapters.title: Corvane's Deadline
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her firm moves up the acquisition timeline and hints at legal pressure on Rafael's café lease. Emotional beat: complicity dawning — Marisol realizes she is the weapon aimed at Rafael.

chapters.title: The Café on the Line
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Corvane buys the café's building; eviction looms unless Rafael signs the orchard away. Emotional beat: cornered fury, loyalty to her staff versus pride.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Terms
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A screaming confrontation unearths why Marisol left a decade ago: her family's debts and her father's ultimatum. Emotional beat: truth as excavation, painful but clearing ground.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Visit
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol quietly inflates the orchard's valuation in her report, her first act of sabotage against her employer. Emotional beat: the first irreversible betrayal of duty for love.

chapters.title: Bread and Evidence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael discovers Marisol's altered appraisal and misreads it as manipulation to lower her buyout price. Emotional beat: misunderstanding weaponized by insecurity.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Rafael signs preliminary papers to sell; Marisol, hurt, stops fighting. Emotional beat: mutual retreat, the coldest chapter, love mistaken for betrayal twice over.

chapters.title: Her Father's House
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts her father, learning he engineered the Corvane deal partly to punish her grandmother's family for an old feud. Emotional beat: power revealed as inherited corruption.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A second hidden letter from Grandmother reveals the feud's origin — a stolen recipe, a stolen love — and asks Rafael to choose differently than the women before her. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as invitation.

chapters.title: Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol copies Corvane's fraudulent documents and contacts the town council and a journalist, knowing it ends her career. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the zoning hearing, Marisol testifies against Corvane and her father; Rafael arrives mid-testimony and publicly withdraws her sale signature. Emotional beat: climax — both risk everything simultaneously, publicly, for each other.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Corvane retaliates; the café closes its doors for good, and Rafael grieves it honestly with her staff. Emotional beat: loss acknowledged rather than denied — growth made visible.

chapters.title: Cider and Confession
chapters.summary: Both POVs. In the empty orchard kitchen, Rafael offers the whole heart she once withheld; Marisol admits she came back for Rafael long before the deed. Emotional beat: full mutual surrender, quiet after the storm.

chapters.title: Rebuilding on Stubborn Ground
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Plans drawn for a bakery-and-cider house on the orchard; the community, moved by the hearing, invests small amounts. Emotional beat: hope as collective act.

chapters.title: The First Morning
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Opening day: ovens lit, cider pressed, Marisol's father watching from the road, unforgiven but no longer in control. Emotional beat: earned joy, power renounced.

chapters.title: A Songbook for the Bakery
chapters.summary: Both POVs closing together. Rafael pins the biscuit-tin deed framed above the counter beside grandmother's recipe cards; they sing badly while the first customers queue. Emotional beat: resolution — love kept in present tense at last.
